items.title: Frank Chace Interview, 1961-11-18
items.q: I like Noon's work enormously... Noon is a model for clarinet players... I think so. Aesthetically speaking, yes

ctx.x: Well, they talked constantly of having made the tour of the south side, and do you think that it was an overall impression then, rather than a note-for-note imitative desire?

Bud Jacobson told me once that he knew Pee-wee in the late 20s, and that Pee-wee would listen to a record of Jimmy Noon's with his Apex Club Orchestra. I know that you know, which, of course, as everybody knows, has enormously fleet, low register work on it. And Pee-wee tried to imitate the choruses, every note. Now, in that connection, we know this much that Pee-wee deliberately tried to imitate Noon. All I can say is I'm very happy that he failed. I like Noon's work enormously, but I would much less rather have…

Noon, in some respects, was superficial, and there was so much embroidery to his playing that sometimes either the melodic content or the hot content or the rhythm got lost in frills. Now, the frills generally were well-
